precepts.text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him: that's us, the Israelites, before Esau and the nations that made no account of our labours. When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation: the chariots, and us being taken up; that is going to be strange and foreign to them. That is going to be the new talk of the town: a black God and a black Christ coming to redeem his people. And they repenting shall say, This was he whom we had sometimes in derision: how is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints!
precepts.point: And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army. There it is: gathered together, minds already persuaded. And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet, and these both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Revelation says the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies were gathered together to make war against him that sits on the horse. Wisdom shows what happens when they see him: “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” That is us, the Israelites, standing before Esau and the nations, who made no account of our labours here.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” The strangeness of his salvation is the chariots, us being taken up. That is going to be strange and foreign to them. They will no longer talk about the deliverance out of Egypt, but about the new deliverance from the land of the north. A black God, a black Christ, coming to redeem his black people: that is going to be the new talk of the town.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach.” Christ is going to put it in their mind: these are the people you afflicted, raped, robbed, murdered and enslaved. These are my people.

“We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints! Therefore have we erred from the way of truth.”

precepts.text: The righteous man stands in great boldness before those who afflicted him; they are troubled with terrible fear and amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all they looked for.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. Jeremiah 4:7, the lion is come up from his thicket, the destroyer of the Gentiles, Nebuchadnezzar contextually and Christ prophetically. 2 Esdras 11:37, a roaring lion chased out of the wood sends a man's voice unto the eagle, America.
precepts.why:
The Lord is a defence from heat for them that love him, and in that day they will stand. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” Why does he stand in boldness? Because he feared the Lord and stayed faithful.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear”. When the nations see it they will be troubled, saying, what the hell is this? They “shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” They cannot imagine it; they will not be able to fathom what is taking place when those chariots come.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach: We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints!”

The ones who mocked and afflicted the righteous will see him numbered among the children of God, protected while they are not.

precepts.text: The righteous live for evermore; there is no death to the righteous, and our brothers and sisters whose bodies returned to dust are coming back. They shall receive a glorious kingdom on earth, New Jerusalem, and a beautiful crown, 2 Esdras 2:42-45. He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour, and make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies, the leviathan against the navy; righteousness as a breastplate, true judgment instead of an helmet, holiness for an invincible shield, his severe wrath sharpened for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the unwise. Right-aiming thunderbolts shall fly to the mark, hailstones as in Joshua's day, the sea shall rage and the flood drown them, a mighty wind shall blow them away; thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill dealing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. That is what we wait for, preparing our hearts, minds, and souls.
precepts.point: The Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, not all nations. As for me, this is my covenant with them: my spirit that is upon thee, the Holy Spirit, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, the Bible, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor thy seed's seed, from henceforth and for ever.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59 ends with the Lord seeing “that there was no man”, no intercessor, so his own arm brought salvation: Christ “put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing.” “The Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob”: not all nations. And his covenant is his spirit upon us and his words in our mouth, and in our children's mouths, and our children's children's, for ever. Wisdom of Solomon shows what that Redeemer brings.

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” There is no death to the righteous. If you are in this truth keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ, you live forever; our brothers and sisters whose bodies returned to the dust, those spirits are coming back. We have to believe that.

“Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand.” The glorious kingdom shall be on earth: that is New Jerusalem. The crown is the one in 2 Esdras 2:42-45: we are going to get crowned with power. “For with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.”

“He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour”: Christ is coming back for war. “And make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies”: that leviathan is going to come out and attack those bastards on the navy. “He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate”, the same as we read in Isaiah 59, “and true judgment instead of an helmet. He shall take holiness for an invincible shield. His severe wrath shall he sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the unwise.”

“Then shall the right aiming thunderbolts go abroad; and from the clouds, as from a well drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark.” Those weapons won't miss; that lightning won't miss. “And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone bow”, like in the time of Joshua, “and the water of the sea shall rage against them”, tsunamis, “and the floods shall cruelly drown them. Yea, a mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a storm shall blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill dealing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.”

That is what we are waiting for: the second coming of Christ. And God would not be just to let the nations off the hook; if he punished his own people, America, England, Japan and Australia will not be unpunished. So while we wait, we must be preparing our hearts, our minds and our souls.

precepts.text: One city against another, one people against another; and then shall my Son be declared.
precepts.point: When city fights city and realm fights realm, the Son shall be declared and rebuke the wicked inventions of the nations.
precepts.why:
“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord”. They “receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand”: the Lord himself is going to place that crown upon you. “With his arm shall he protect them. He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour, and make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies.” Second Esdras shows when that revenge comes.

“Behold, the days come, when the most High will begin to deliver them that are upon the earth. And he shall come to the astonishment of them that dwell on the earth.” Before it, “one shall undertake to fight against another, one city against another, one place against another, one people against another, and one realm against another.” There will be wars one against another, city against city, the same as was read earlier in the class.

“And the time shall be when these things shall come to pass, and the signs shall happen which I shewed thee before, and then shall my Son be declared”: then Christ shall be declared. He is not coming back as a regular man that anyone can do harm to; he is coming back with his army. An innumerable multitude gathers “willing to come, and to overcome him by fighting. But he shall stand upon the top of the mount Sion.”

“And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest”. He lays before them “their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame”, and he destroys them without labour. That is the end of the war of the gods, and the reward of the righteous who live for evermore.
